title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming formatting
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions to parity with OpenAI semantics for request params, role handling, stop sequences, and logprobs while improving streaming stability and preserving structured output/function-call behavior. This PR addresses differences observed in real customer workloads and fixes edge cases exposed by our compatibility test suite. Changes: 1) Request params normalization: accept both single string and list forms for 'stop'; support 'temperature', 'top_p', 'max_tokens' mapping to internal runtime params; propagate 'logprobs' request to token-scoring path. 2) Role canonicalization: normalize system/user/assistant role labels, preserve custom role content when provided, and ensure role-indexing for prefix/KV cache. 3) Stop/logprobs: implement multi-string stop detection in streaming path and ensure final token logprobs are returned consistent with batch sync responses. 4) Response formatting: ensure function/tool call structured output is emitted as a single assistant message with 'function_call' metadata per OpenAI shape; string escape/JSON serialization fixes for nested structured output. 5) Streaming stability: avoid duplicate final chunks, introduce idempotent chunk emission, and add retry-safe resume tokens for client reconnects. Migration notes: compatibility layer maps OpenAI-style params to our runtime defaults; no customer-facing breaking changes expected but clients relying on previously buggy logprob behavior may see differences. Testing: added integration harness tests that run both streaming and sync paths against the OpenAI parity fixture set and updated goldens. Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests added [x] docs updated [x] e2e perf verified on staging -- See related Linear tasks ENG-1245 and ENG-1302 for rollout plan and metrics to monitor.
commits_summary: 8 commits: initial mapping for params and roles; implement stop detector in streaming manager; wire logprob passthrough to token-scorer; function_call formatting fixes; add integration tests and goldens; add retry-safe resume token; perf tweaks for prefix handling; docs and changelog.
diff_snippets: gateway/openai_compat.py: added mapping for stop param: if isinstance(stop, str): stop = [stop]
runtime/streaming_manager.rs: added final_chunk_dedup flag and resume_token generation for reconnect-safe streaming
sdk/python/openai_compat.py: assemble response object with choices[0].message and choices[0].finish_reason matching OpenAI shape

Maya Chen: I'm worried about KV cache index changes affecting throughput. Can we gate the canonicalization behind a toggle? Asha: added a runtime flag 'compat.role_canonicalization' default true; performance regression on staging was <2% after tweaks
Ravi Singh: CI flakes on macOS-lint looked unrelated, re-ran. Approving after green CI.
testing_notes: Added parity fixture runner that replays OpenAI-style conversation payloads against both sync and streaming endpoints and compares JSON-normalized outputs. New tests cover: role normalization, multiple stop tokens split across chunks, logprobs presence in final streaming event, and function_call structured output formatting.
release_notes: - OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: request param handling (stop list/string, temperature/top_p/max_tokens) standardized. - Role handling: system/user/assistant canonicalization for improved compatibility and KV-cache correctness. - Stop sequences: multi-string stop detection in streaming fixed. - Logprobs: token-level logprobs are now returned consistently for streaming and sync responses when requested. - Structured output: function/tool call formatting now matches OpenAI shape to improve SDK interop.
post_merge_actions: Deploy compatibility flag to Canary cluster, monitor parity metrics (ENG-1245) for 48h, enable global rollout if error-rate and latency stable. Update public docs page and API changelog.
notes: This PR was driven by customer reports and internal parity tests that surfaced multiple discrepancies. Coordinated with SDK teams to ensure the Python and TypeScript wrappers preserve OpenAI-shaped responses. No schema-breaking changes expected for existing Redwood API users.
